sa_market_summary: The Mercedes-Benz C-Class W205 (2014-2021) is the most common used luxury sedan in South Africa. Its design, build quality, and brand perception make it highly aspirational for middle-market buyers. However, the C-Class is one of the most maintenance-intensive vehicles in the SA used market ,  out-of-warranty examples can generate significant unexpected costs. The C220d diesel is the most practical variant for SA conditions due to fuel economy. Any buyer must budget carefully for running costs beyond the sticker price.

known_faults.fault: Air suspension and ABC system failure (AMG/high spec variants)
known_faults.description: The Active Body Control and air suspension components on high-spec W205 variants are expensive to maintain. Strut replacement and system leaks are the most common issues.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check the car sits level. Listen for any air compressor noise from the boot. Request any suspension work history.
known_faults.source: Mercedes SA dealer service data, SA independent Merc specialists

known_faults.description: The 7G-Tronic automatic gearbox can develop jerking, hunting between gears, and delayed engagement. The valve body and conductor plate are the most common failure points. Very expensive to repair.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Test drive with focus on smooth gear changes. Any hesitation or jerk between gears is a red flag. Request transmission service history ,  fluid change is critical every 60,000km.
known_faults.source: Mercedes SA dealer technical reports, SA gearbox specialist data

known_faults.fault: NOx sensor and AdBlue system failure (C220d)
known_faults.description: The C220d diesel uses AdBlue (DEF) fluid for emissions. NOx sensors, AdBlue pumps, and SCR catalysts can fail. A warning light preventing engine start is a common symptom.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check AdBlue level and quality. Request NOx sensor replacement history. A full diagnostic scan will reveal any stored emissions fault codes.
known_faults.source: Mercedes SA diesel technical bulletins, SA diesel specialist reports

known_faults.description: Some W205 petrol engines consume oil between service intervals. Mercedes-Benz considers up to 1L per 1,000km acceptable ,  many SA buyers do not.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check the oil dipstick ,  compare to the full mark. Ask the seller how often oil is topped up between services. Any consumption above 0.5L per 1,000km is concerning.
known_faults.estimated_repair_zar: R0 (top up) to R35,000+ (piston ring replacement)
known_faults.source: Mercedes SA technical service notes, MyBroadband Merc forum

known_faults.fault: Sunroof and panoramic roof drain blockage
known_faults.description: Blocked sunroof drainage channels cause water to pool above the headliner and drain into the footwells. Electrical damage including ECU water ingress is a serious risk.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check footwells for damp carpet. Check under the rear seat bench. Open and close the sunroof and listen for any water movement.
known_faults.estimated_repair_zar: R500 (drain cleaning) to R15,000+ (ECU or electrical damage repair)
known_faults.source: SA auto electricians, Mercedes SA owner community

known_faults.description: The COMAND infotainment system can develop screen freezes, Bluetooth connectivity issues, and navigation failures. Software updates from Mercedes resolve many issues.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Test all infotainment functions. Check Bluetooth pairing, navigation, and screen response time.
known_faults.source: Mercedes SA dealer software update records, SA owner forums

what_to_inspect_before_buying: Full Mercedes-Benz Star Diagnostic scan ,  non-negotiable
Check gearbox for smooth shifting through all seven ratios
Test air conditioning ,  check for any compressor noise
Inspect all door seals and sunroof drains for water ingress
Check for oil consumption by inspecting dipstick at time of viewing
Verify Mercedes SA service history with dealer stamps
Request an independent inspection from a Merc specialist before purchase
Budget minimum R25,000 per year for maintenance beyond normal services
Confirm no outstanding recalls ,  Mercedes SA frequently issues safety recalls
owner_sentiment: Mixed. C-Class owners love the prestige, interior quality, and driving experience. Many report significant frustration with unexpected repair costs, particularly on out-of-warranty examples. The common SA advice: never buy a C-Class you cannot afford to fix. The C220d diesel owners report better ownership experiences due to lower service frequency.
